# GPU Sandbox Pricing: Modal vs Daytona vs Thunder Compute (2026)

GPU sandbox pricing compared: an H100 sandbox costs $2.95 to $3.95/hr at Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona. See full per-second rates and real costs.

Carl Peterson · Updated Nov 05, 2026 · 10 min Read

H100 GPU sandboxes start at $2.95/hr on Thunder Compute and cost up to $3.95/hr on Modal and Daytona's on-demand tier. Daytona also offers cheaper preemptible rates, but sandboxes can be terminated without notice. All three platforms charge separately for vCPUs and memory; GPU rates are only part of the bill.

This guide breaks down the GPU sandbox bill and the rules that affect the total. Base prices were last reviewed in October 2026, before volume discounts or region multipliers.

...

- vCPU and memory add $0.92-1.34/hr to a sandbox for 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory.
- Full configurations at base rates range from $3.20/hr (Daytona preemptible) to $5.29/hr (Modal).
- Per second billing is the standard among covered providers.
- Preemptible GPU sandboxes cost less but can be terminated without notice.
- Modal with narrow region selection costs 2.4x more than Thunder Compute for the example configuration ($9.25/hr vs $3.88/hr).

## What a GPU Sandbox Actually Costs per Hour

A realistic H100 GPU sandbox costs $3.20-$5.29/hr across these options once CPU and memory are included. This cost table prices one H100 with 8 vCPUs, 32 GiB of memory and 100 GiB of storage at list rates.

Daytona preemptible sandboxes have the lowest hourly rate if runs survive. Evicted runs must be paid for again. At base rates, Thunder Compute is about 20% cheaper than Daytona on-demand and 27% cheaper than Modal for this configuration.

...

### CPU, Memory and Storage on Top of the GPU

All three platforms bill GPU, CPU and memory for as long as a sandbox runs. Thunder Compute and Daytona also bill storage; Modal does not bill Sandbox disk separately. On Thunder Compute and Daytona, 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory add $0.92/hr to an H100 sandbox. On Modal, the same resources cost $1.34/hr.

Resource sizing matters as much as the GPU choice. Thunder Compute and Daytona bill the vCPUs and memory you configure. Modal bills whichever is higher, your request or actual usage.

...

### Egress: Modal's New Network Charge

Modal started charging for network egress on October 1, 2026. Modal's egress billing charges $0.04/GiB once a workspace uses its allowance for the billing cycle:

- Starter: 1 TiB included
- Team: 10 TiB included
- Enterprise: 100 TiB included

Egress covers traffic leaving a container's network interface, including private traffic to other Modal containers and uploads through Cloud Bucket Mounts. Reads from and writes to Modal Volumes don't count.

results.author: Carl Peterson
highlights:
Carl Peterson · Updated Oct 07, 2026 · 11 min Read

- GPU sandboxes give untrusted, agent-generated code a real GPU behind an isolation boundary.
- Most AI sandboxes are CPU-only, because stock Firecracker doesn't support GPU passthrough.
- Three isolation paths exist: VFIO passthrough (Daytona), gVisor (Modal) and Firecracker microVMs with custom GPU support (Thunder Compute).
- Preemption, GPU range and persistence separate the three managed GPU sandbox platforms.
- Thunder Compute's H100 sandboxes cost $2.95/hr and are never preempted.

...

Three managed platforms offer GPUs inside the sandbox itself: Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona. Separate GPU inference APIs don't qualify, because the GPU sits outside the sandbox. The three platforms differ enough on GPU range, preemption and persistence to decide most choices. Details in the comparison table were verified in October 2026.

...

### Non-Preemptible GPU Sandboxes with H100s at $2.95 per Hour

Thunder Compute's H100 sandboxes cost $2.95 per hour, billed per second. An H100 costs $3.95/hr at Modal and as an on-demand H100 at Daytona. Every Thunder Compute sandbox is non-preemptible, so long evals and RL runs aren't evicted partway through.

# Best GPU Sandboxes for AI Agents (2026)

Compare the best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026. Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal ranked on GPU types, preemption, isolation and H100 price.

Carl Peterson · Updated Oct 07, 2026 · 7 min Read

The best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026 are Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal. Thunder Compute offers the lowest on-demand H100 rate of the three. Daytona offers flexible hardware and cheaper spot capacity. Modal has the widest GPU range, from T4 to B300, on a broader serverless platform.

Most agent sandboxes are CPU-only, and only a few sandbox platforms put a GPU inside the sandbox itself. This guide compares three managed GPU sandbox platforms, with verified prices and limits.

Takeaways

- Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.95/hr.
- Daytona offers the most flexibility, with eight GPU types and spot capacity.
- Modal has the widest GPU range, from T4 to B300, but its GPU sandboxes are preemptible only.
- E2B and Vercel Sandbox are CPU-only, so they don't qualify as GPU sandboxes.

...

Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal all bill per second and charge vCPU, memory and storage on top of the GPU rate. The comparison table shows how the three platforms differ on GPUs, price, preemption and persistence.

## 1. Thunder Compute: Non-Preemptible H100s at the Lowest On-Demand Rate

Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.95/hr against $3.95/hr at Modal and Daytona on-demand. Every Thunder Compute sandbox is non-preemptible. Long evals and RL runs finish at the quoted price instead of being evicted and rerun.

Each Thunder Compute sandbox is a Firecracker microVM (a lightweight, hardware-isolated VM). Sandboxes are created through a Python SDK. Commands run as durable jobs, and outbound network access can be open, blocked or restricted to allowlists.

Best for: long evals, RL rollouts and inference loops where interruptions are costly.
